messages.subject: Security gone when using index.html instead of ui.R
messages.subject_clean: Security gone when using index.html instead of ui.R
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

I have a few apps up & running with security in place (login + pwd) as per the tutorial working fine. Now, I have designed this new app, and this time I got rid off the ui.R and create the whole front-end using www/index.html. The apps work fines (apart from some quirks in googlevis calendar) but I noticed I don't get prompt for login + pwd anymore.

Is this something anyone else has come across before? and more importantly are there any solutions or workarounds?

Many thanks,

Alberto

messages.body_plain:
Hi Juan,
Not sure where your issue lies, but if you do the following, you should be able to upload your application pretty easily hopefully.

- Go to the directory that contains your .rmd file
- run:  shinyapps::deployApp()

The directory you are in will be sent up to the server and if you only have that one app in the directory it should open a browser window right to it.

-Tareef

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] default account
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] default account
messages.body_plain:
Hi Tareef,

I can't see your reply in the thread, just in my emails...

You're right!
The app directory contains a shinyapps subdir with 2 dirs inside: one named with my old account, and one with my new account.
Both contain its own .dcf with the same app name, but the corresponding account name, bundleId and url.

Suppressing an account do not remove the corresponding subdir and .dcf in apps.
I removed the old one manually, and everything works fine.

Fred

messages.body_plain:
Hi Ali,

Thanks a lot for simplifying your app and showing the source code!
That is a great step forward. However, when I tried to run your app, I
got all sorts of problems, such as the missing introduction.html in
includeHTML("introduction.html"). Could you please further simplify it
to a minimal, self-contained, and reproducible example? There are
quite a few things that I think can be removed, such as the progress
bar from shinyIncubator. Are all of tm, fastcluster, gsl, and
topicmodels required to reproduce the problem? If not, please remove
as many add-on packages as you can. Similarly, are all UI components
absolutely needed?...

Regards,
Yihui
--
Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com>
Web: http://yihui.name

>

>
> In addition to the problem described above in a sample app (that stemming
> removes all character data - presumably this may be an encoding issue. But I

>
> This is the link to this new app: https://kazmialiarsalan.shinyapps.io/test/

>
> We may focus on this original problem - I shared the other problem because

How can I make the js files readable to shinyApps?

The whole code is too long, the parts involved are:

server.R
json <- readLines("br-states.js")

ui.R
includeHTML("mapa.js")

If someone want to see my app draft: https://psuantt.shinyapps.io/Consolidado/    (the map is the last tab)

Thanks in advance!!

Luis Otavio

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] encoding error on upload of Shiny App--related to earlier questions from Windows users?
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] encoding error on upload of Shiny App--related to earlier questions from Windows users?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Kevin,

I looked into this issue and it turns out that it has nothing to do
with encoding. The current error message is too vague about where
exactly the error comes from. I just added a more informative message
to shinyapps. After you devtools::install_github('rstudio/shinyapps'),
you will realize the real problem:

Preparing to deploy application...DONE
Uploading application bundle...

* Failed to parse /home/yihui/tmp/shiny-app2-master/scratch 16 Aug 2014.R

Error in parse(input, n = -1L, encoding = checkEncoding(file)) :
  11:7: unexpected symbol
10:     sidebarPanel
11:       selectInput
          ^

Calls: <Anonymous> ... append -> fileDependencies ->
withCallingHandlers -> parse
Execution halted

So the problem is that you have an R script 'scratch 16 Aug 2014.R'
that is not a syntactically valid script. The reason that shinyapps
tries to parse this R script is that it actually parses all R scripts
in the app to figure out the package dependencies (e.g. you might have
library(foo) in bar.R and you source('bar.R') in server.R).

You can either remove this invalid R script from your app, or make it
a syntactically valid script.

Regards,
Yihui
--
Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com>
Web: http://yihui.name

messages.subject: [9/5/2014] ShinyApps update
messages.subject_clean: [9/5/2014] ShinyApps update
messages.body_plain:
Dear ShinyApps users,

We are happy to announce improvements to the shinyapps.io <https://www.shinyapps.io/> service over the past few weeks. These include:

Support for BioConductor-based packages

Speed improvements on first-time builds of your applications

Support for more concurrent connections

Support for R packages that require the quantlib library

BioConductor support

You can now use your favorite packages from BioConductor and deploy them to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>. Simply take any locally running shiny application or R markdown <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com> document and deploy it via deployApp(). The shinyapps package you create will identify the dependencies and pass them along to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>.

Note: You will need to upgrade to the latest version of the shinyapps package by running the R command:

devtools::install_github(“rstudio/shinyapps”)

Faster build times

The time it takes for an app to deploy the first time has been improved significantly due to improved caching of packages.  For the most common packages used, the performance of the build is now almost 5x faster. This improvement took effect last week. You don’t need to do anything to take advantage of it. Most app deployments are just faster now!

More concurrent connections per application

We have increased the limit on the number of concurrent connections that can be handled by an R process from 20 to 100.

Quantlib support

For users interested in using libraries like RQuantLib <http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/RQuantLib/index.html>, shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> now bundles the underlying quantlib libraries into the core of the service making that possible.

Thank you all for your help in improving the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io/> platform.  We hope you like these enhancements and we look forward to your feedback as always.

Best,

The ShinyApps team

messages.body_plain:
Hi Yihui,

Please accept my many thanks for your help! The problem has been solved!

You were correct in pointing out that the error (invalid multibyte string at '<97> as t) was due to inappropriate encoding.

However, it weren't the data sets that produced this problem, but (what I should have suspected much before) the about.html and introduction.html files! I was using an Em Dash and a 'ü' - these characters caused the problem.

I tried loading the HTML with the appropriate UTF-8 encoding, but the problem remained. For the time being, I simply removed the Em dash, and the character. Later, I will look into whether I was loading the encoding properly or not.

The functional application can be found at this link: https://kazmialiarsalan.shinyapps.io/QualitativeAnalysisApp-R/

Once again, thanks for teaching me how to test apps properly! I was being lazy, since I had been working on this app for quite some time. Not an excuse, though!

>

> should have suspected much before) the about.html and introduction.html
> files! I was using an Em Dash and a 'ü' - these characters caused the
> problem.
>
> I tried loading the HTML with the appropriate UTF-8 encoding, but the
> problem remained. For the time being, I simply removed the Em dash, and the
> character. Later, I will look into whether I was loading the encoding
> properly or not.
>
> The functional application can be found at this link:
> https://kazmialiarsalan.shinyapps.io/QualitativeAnalysisApp-R/
>
> Once again, thanks for teaching me how to test apps properly! I was being
> lazy, since I had been working on this app for quite some time. Not an
> excuse, though!
>

messages.subject_clean: App deploys successfully but I get "ERROR: cannot open the connection"
messages.body_plain:
I think Shiny is a great platform and look forward to using it quite a bit in the future.  I've deployed two apps thus far (just testing everything out) but today when I tried to deploy an app that runs successfully locally, I get "ERROR: cannot open the connection" after the app is deployed.

I can't tell what's wrong: everything is in the working directory, including the sourced function and I received no errors during deployment. Output from deployApp() is:

> deployApp()
Preparing to deploy application...DONE
Uploading application bundle...DONE
Deploying application: 19458...
Waiting for task: 1407047
  building: Building image: 48851
  building: Installing packages
  building: Installing files
  building: Pushing image: 48851
  deploying: Starting instances
  rollforward: Activating new instances
  terminating: Stopping old instances
Application successfully deployed to http://stevenranney.shinyapps.io/craps

The address is stevenranney.shinyapps.io/craps <http://stevenranney.shinyapps.io/craps>

Any help?  This is mostly a learning exercise for me so not truly important in the grand scheme of things but I'm curious as to why it's not deploying successfully.

Thanks -

SR

messages.subject: How to determine memory usage in a shiny app?
messages.subject_clean: How to determine memory usage in a shiny app?
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
 I have an up on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> and it works fine on my desktop and usually works fine on shinyapps. From time to time, however, it grays out but only on shinyapps and not in a way which I can reproduce. My thought was that this might be a issue related to memory usage. I know how to increase my memory size on shinyapps, but I don't know how to find out how much I need. Is there any way to monitor memory usage for an app?
Thanks
 JP

Another possibility may be that the application is going to sleep due to inactivity, is that possible?

messages.subject: Re: 答复: [shinyapps-users] Re: application unexpectedly exit due to my css style
messages.subject_clean: 答复: [shinyapps-users] Re: application unexpectedly exit due to my css style
messages.body_plain:
It depends on where you are storing the data Wen.  Our recommendation would be for you to write it to a location that you have read access to from the outside since writes to disk are not guaranteed to be persisted.

Options to consider:
- Write the data from the user to a database you have access to.  This could be a database in the cloud (Amazon's RDS, MongoLabs, Cloudant, Google Cloud SQL, or any number of cloud hosted databases), or it could be your own database where you open a connection to the outside world for the purposes of getting this data in there.
- Write the data to a file or data store you have access to.  You could "FTP" the data somewhere, or potentially store it in an S3 bucket that only you have access to.

Hope this helps
-Tareef

messages.body_plain:
This a repeat of a question in the shiny discussion group but probably makes more sense here

I want to hide my code but echo=FALSE does not work for a reactive

```{r, echo = FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggvis)
library(dplyr)

selectInput("category", "Choose Dataset:", c("mpg", "disp", "qsec"))

testCode <- max(mtcars$mpg)

# ggvis with dynamically changing columns
reactive({
  if (!is.null(input$category))
    col <- input$category
  else
    col <- "mpg"

  mtcars %>% ggvis(~mpg, ~disp)

}) %>% bind_shiny('foo')

ggvisOutput('foo')
```

The selectInput and ggvis chart show as required and the testCode line is hidden but I get

## reactive({
##     if (!is.null(input$category))
##         col <- input$category
##     else col <- "mpg"
##     mtcars %>% ggvis(~mpg, ~disp)
## })

on the page , which is not desired

TIA

messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] audio element in Shiny
messages.body_plain:
That is also my guess. Files under the root directory of the app will
not be found by direct links, which might be a little surprising... In
shiny, you can put files under www/ and link to them without the www
prefix, e.g. for an app with files

ui.R
server.R
www/foo.wav
bar.wav

You can link to foo.wav by tags$a(href = 'foo.wav', 'foo') (or
tags$audio(src = 'foo.wav')) but tags$a(href = 'bar.wav') will not
work by default, unless you used shiny::addResourcePath().

Anyway, when something does not work, you first see if there are error
messages in the R console, then Ctrl + Shift + J in Google Chrome to
see if there are error messages in the browser console. For apps
deployed to ShinyApps.io, shinyapps::showLogs() is what might help
you. (To Garret: we probably should add these common techniques for
diagnosing shiny apps to
http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/debugging.html)

Regards,
Yihui
--
Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com>

messages.body_plain:
When an app does not work in the web browser, the first thing you can
do is to open the JavaScript console (e.g. in Google Chrome, Ctrl +
Shift + J) and see if there are error messages. In your case, the
error message is:

[blocked] The page at 'https://demo.shinyapps.io/shiny-test/' was
loaded over HTTPS, but ran insecure content from
'http://www.arcgis.com/home/webmap/embedViewer.html?webmap=f7535ebbb05b4eaf8…36&displayslider=true&displayscalebar=true&displaydetails=true':
this content should also be loaded over HTTPS.

This is because ShinyApps.io uses HTTPS to host apps, so normal HTTP
resources will not work (e.g. http://www.arcgis.com).

After I replaced http://www.arcgis.com with //www.arcgis.com <http://www.arcgis.com> (this is
called "Protocol relative url"; see
http://stackoverflow.com/q/9161769/559676) and deployed the app to
ShinyApps, the background map showed up. Then you have to work out the
rest of issues, since there seem to be many, many errors in the
JavaScript console, which are not relevant to Shiny or ShinyApps.io.
These errors also show up when the app is running locally. Sorry I'm
not familiar with arcgis.com <http://arcgis.com> so I cannot help further.

Regards,
Yihui
--

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Shiny Server definition of "R process per application"
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Shiny Server definition of "R process per application"
messages.body_plain:
Hi John,
You can absolutely have multiple users using a single application at the same time on Shiny Server. The single threaded nature of R means that if you have an application that takes some time to complete some computation, the other users would have to wait for that work to complete before their work starts.
With ShinyApps.io, we do start multiple R processes and with the new subscription tiers we offer we will provide tools that give the publisher greater control over the number of R processes per application.
